definition: Visual Flight Rules - rules that govern flight under visual meteorological conditions.
Visual Meteorological Conditions - weather conditions expressed in terms of visibility, distance from clouds, and ceiling.
Indicated Airspeed - the airspeed shown on the aircraft airspeed indicator.
Federal Aviation Administration - the U.S. agency responsible for civil aviation safety and regulation.
Air Traffic Control - the service responsible for managing aircraft separation and traffic flow in controlled airspace.
Private Pilot Licence / Private Pilot License - the certification for private operation of aircraft.
Meteorological Aerodrome Report - an aviation routine weather report issued at regular intervals.
Terminal Aerodrome Forecast - a forecast of expected weather conditions for a specific airport area.
Commercial Pilot Licence / Commercial Pilot License - a licence allowing operation for remuneration or hire under relevant rules.
Airman's Meteorological Information - a weather advisory for hazardous conditions that may affect VFR operations.
Significant Meteorological Information - a weather advisory concerning significant hazardous conditions such as severe turbulence or icing.
Instrument Flight Rules - rules governing flight by reference to instruments instead of external visual cues.
Missed Approach Point - the point on an instrument approach where a missed approach procedure begins if required criteria are not met.
Non-Directional Beacon - a radio navigation beacon from which bearings are obtained relative to the station.
Very High Frequency Omni-Directional Range - a radio navigation aid used for bearing and course guidance.
